en.text:
## Instructions
---

@[card: Follow me](https://civitai.com/user/lonecatone23)

@[card: Follow me](https://www.instagram.com/synth.studio.models/)

@[card: Get my stuff here](https://github.com/lonecatone23)

@[card: Get my models here](https://huggingface.co/Lonecatone23)


@[card: Buy me a ☕](https://ko-fi.com/lonecatone)

### This is many hours of work. If you enjoy it, please 👍 like, 💬 comment, and feel free to ⚡ tip 😉

---

### 🛑🚫✋ What this workflow is for
- A test bench for two new nodes: **LC Sigmas** and **LC Detail Daemon**. Same prompt, same model, run two ways, and the comparer shows you the difference.
- **Top path (new):** LC Sigmas builds the schedule, LC Detail Daemon adds detail, and two samplers split the work (high pass, then low pass).
- **Bottom path (baseline):** a plain KSampler on euler / simple. This is "what you would normally get".
- Every setting here came out of a 3,432 image test across Krea 2 Turbo and Raw, Z-Image, Flux 2 Klein, SDXL and Illustrious.

---

**LC Sigmas (BETA) 📉**
- A sigma is just how much noise is left at a step. The schedule is the list of those amounts, start to finish. Big noise = the model decides the big stuff (pose, composition, light). Small noise = fine detail (skin, hair, fabric).
- **preset auto (from model)** reads which model you loaded and fills in the sampler and shape that tested best for it (Krea 2: euler + beta57). Pick a model family to fill them in right away. Change the shape or sampler yourself and it switches to manual. The green line under the graph tells you what tested best.
- The graph shows your schedule: orange = high pass, blue = low pass, dashed = the model's plain schedule for comparison. It updates live once you have run it.
- **handoff** splits the render into two passes. 0 = one pass. A second model (model_2) can take the low pass, and the low pass always starts at exactly the noise level where the high pass stopped (no jump).
- **renoise** gives the low pass a little extra noise to work with. This is the one for cleaning up ControlNet: the clean model gets room to wash out what the ControlNet model left.
- **denoise** is for image to image. The info line tells you the real starting noise, because on Krea 2 "denoise 0.5" actually starts at 76% noise.
- It also outputs the noise for each pass and the sampler, so you do not need RandomNoise, DisableNoise or KSamplerSelect nodes.

**LC Detail Daemon (BETA) 😈**
- Adds detail by telling the model there is a little less noise than there really is, so it removes a little less and keeps more fine texture.
- **amount** is a plain percentage: 0.08 = 8% of the noise is hidden from the model at the peak. It is *not* multiplied by your CFG like the old Detail Daemon.
- **start / end** are how far along the image is (0% = pure noise, 100% = finished), so they land in the same place no matter how many steps or passes you run.
- **mode auto** picks the right method for the model. The classic Detail Daemon method actually works *backwards* on Krea 2 (hazy at 0.10, blocks at 0.20). Auto fixes that, so positive always means more detail.
- It sits on the high pass only. Want detail later in the render too? Wire it into the low pass sampler as well.
- ⚠️ Samplers that add their own noise (dpmpp_2m_sde, euler_ancestral, er_sde) plus Detail Daemon leave pepper specks. Halve the amount with those, or stay on euler.

**Baseline**
- Plain KSampler, euler / simple. Compare it against the new path in the image comparer and judge for yourself.

---

***"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"***- Yoda Auditore, *Assassin's Wars*

nodes.title: Your Prompt (if not using LC Vision or adding to it)

widgets_values: Describe this image in detail: the subject's appearance, pose, and expression, their clothing, the setting and background, lighting and color palette, composition, and overall mood.

You are a helpful vision assistant. Describe what you are shown in rich, concrete detail rather than a brief summary: subject appearance, pose and expression, clothing, setting and background, lighting, color palette, composition and camera angle, and overall mood. Do not skip detail for the sake of brevity. Respond with the final answer only -- no reasoning, no <think> blocks.

properties.lc_display_text:
A woman with long, dark, wavy hair styled in a thick braid over her right shoulder. She wears a wide-brimmed brown cowboy hat with a decorative band around the crown. Her facial expression is neutral to slightly serious, with direct eye contact and lips parted slightly. She has prominent, well-defined eyebrows and noticeable makeup including eyeliner and dark lipstick.

Her attire consists of a black sleeveless top that ends at her waist, paired with faded blue denim jeans secured by a brown leather belt featuring an ornate, circular metal buckle. Her left arm is heavily tattooed with intricate designs: a large portrait of a woman in a cowboy hat surrounded by roses, skulls, and cacti; stars; horseshoes; and other western-themed imagery including a depiction of a horseman on her forearm.

She is seated on a weathered wooden fence post or similar structure. To her right, a portion of an ornate brown leather saddle with fringes is visible, suggesting a rodeo or cowboy setting. The background features a vast, arid landscape under a pale sky, with distant mountains faintly discernible through the haze.

The lighting is natural and diffused, casting soft shadows that define the contours of her body and the textures of her clothing and tattoos. The color palette is dominated by earthy tones: browns, grays, and muted blues, punctuated by the stark black ink of the tattoos and the subtle highlights on her skin.

The composition centers on the subject, capturing a three-quarter view as she leans back slightly with one arm resting on the fence, creating an image that feels both posed for the camera and grounded in a realistic setting. The overall mood is rugged, authentic, and evocative of classic American frontier or western themes.

nodes.title: Notes:

en.text:
## LC Vision Caption 📝

**LC Vision Loader 🔬**:
- ⚠️ This auto downloads the model you choose on the first run, so it will take several minutes.
- The model selector shows your already downloaded options as well as available downloads.

**LC Vision Caption 📝**:
- 💡 The node analyzes the image and detects subject, pose, clothing, setting, lighting, color, composition, and mood, not just a one-line summary.
- Each reference gets its own label (`<Reference 1>`, `<Reference 2>`, `<Reference 3>`), described individually instead of mashed into one blob. 😎
- `style_tag` pushes the description toward a specific visual style regardless of what the reference actually looks like.

**💡 Analyzing 3 images at once**
- Custom prompt: "Analyze <Reference 1>, <Reference 2>, and <Reference 3> individually: describe each one's subject, setting, lighting, and mood. Then compare all three and note the key similarities and differences between them."
- The model addresses each picture by its own label instead of blending them together.

nodes.title: How to use

en.text:
### ✋ How to use

**1. Use I2I 🖼️ (toggle)**
- **Off:** text to image. The empty latent comes from LC Aspect Ratio Simplifier.
- **On:** image to image from **Load Image**. Then set **denoise** on LC Sigmas below 1 (start at 0.6). At 1 your picture gets fully replaced.

**2. LC Aspect Ratio Simplifier 📐**
- Pick a size preset (or custom width / height). This sets the size of everything.

**3. LC Model Optimizer ⚡**
- **base_model:** match your model (Krea 2 Turbo for Krealism).
- **goal:** Optimal is the safe pick. Fast trades a little quality for speed.

**4. Your prompt / Use Prompt Assist 📝 (toggle)**
- Type your prompt in **Your Prompt**.
- **Use Prompt Assist on:** LC Vision describes your loaded image and adds it to your prompt. Off = your prompt only.
- **Final Prompt** shows exactly what gets sent.

**5. LC Seed 🌱**
- One seed for the whole run. Fix it when you compare settings, so only the setting changes.

**6. LC Sigmas 📉**
- **preset:** leave on auto (from model). It fills in the sampler and shape for your model. Changing either one by hand switches it to manual.
- **steps:** total steps for both passes. Krea 2 Turbo: 8. Krea 2 Raw: 28 or more.
- **handoff:** 0 = one pass. For two passes put it near the end (6 of 8).
- **focus:** leave at 0. Negative = more composition, positive = more texture. It changes the look, it does not make it "better".
- **shift:** leave on model.
- **denoise:** 1 for text to image. 0.4 to 0.7 for image to image.
- **renoise:** 0 unless a second model on model_2 is cleaning up (try 0.1).

**7. LC Detail Daemon 😈**
- **amount:** Krea 2 Turbo 0.05 to 0.10 (blocks above 0.2). Krea 2 Raw: leave it off. Z-Image up to 0.15. SDXL 0.05. Illustrious 0.05 to 0.10.
- **start / end:** 0.2 and 0.8 are good. Do not push end past 0.9, the last steps should be left alone.
- **peak:** 0.5 = strongest in the middle of the window.
- **mode:** auto.

**8. Compare**
- The image comparer shows the baseline (A) against the new path (B). Drag across it.

---
